title: 14 Palworld Pals With Partner Skills Worth Using | Mounts, Healing, Base Boosts | Palworld Guide
description: Fourteen Palworld 1.0 Pals whose partner skills change how you play: Fire, Water and Ice mounts, healing, damage boosts, base boosters and explorers. Skills and work levels checked against two Pal databases in November 2026.

sections.heading: 14 Pals with useful partner skills
sections.script: Every Pal in Palworld has a partner skill, and some of them are far better than their rank suggests. In this video we look at fourteen Pals whose partner skills quietly change how you play. Some boost your damage, some heal you, some turn into mounts, and some make your whole base work faster. We checked every name, skill and work level against two separate Pal databases in November twenty twenty six, and we only kept the details where both agreed. Palworld one point zero changed many numbers, so old videos can be out of date. We will not cover breeding here. This one is all about what these Pals do for you once they are on your team. Let us start with the Fire Pals.

sections.heading: Rooby and Pyrin: the Fire pair
sections.script: Rooby is a small Fire Pal with a clever partner skill called Tiny Spark. While Rooby is in your party, the Defense of Fire Pals goes up by fifteen to thirty percent, and the bonus does not stack. At your base, Rooby works Kindling and Farming at level one, and it sometimes drops a Flame Organ when it lives on a Ranch. Pyrin is the bigger brother in this list. Its partner skill, Red Hare, lets you ride it. While you are mounted, your attack type becomes Fire and your Attack rises by five to twenty percent. At base Pyrin is a serious cook, with Kindling at level four, and it also works Lumbering at level two. If you want one Fire Pal for both travel and work, Pyrin is hard to beat.

sections.heading: Water and Ice: Azurobe, Polapup and Foxcicle
sections.script: Now the cold side of the map. Azurobe has a partner skill called Waterwing Dance. It lets you ride across water, and while you are mounted your attack type changes to Water with five to twenty percent more Attack. At base Azurobe is the best Watering worker in this list, at level four. Polapup is the snow specialist. Its skill, Rider of the Snowy Mountain, makes it rideable, with eighty to one hundred sixty percent more movement speed on snow, and you can slide quickly down slopes. At base Polapup works Watering at level three and Cooling at level four. Foxcicle supports your whole Ice team. Its skill, Aurora Guide, raises the Attack of Ice Pals by fifteen to thirty percent while it is in your party. At base it works Cooling at level four and Farming at level three.

sections.heading: Cinnamoth and Petallia: the base boosters
sections.script: Some partner skills do their best work while the Pal is sitting at your base. Cinnamoth is a great example. Its skill, Mysterious Scales, attacks the targeted enemy with Poison Fog when you activate it. While Cinnamoth lives at your base, every other base Pal gets plus one Farming level, and the bonus does not stack. It also works Planting, Gathering and Medicine Production at level two. Petallia is even stronger. When you activate its skill, Blessing of the Flower Spirit, soothing blossoms restore seventy five to eighty five percent of your health. At your base, it adds plus one Planting level to every other base Pal, and that does not stack either. Petallia itself works Planting and Medicine Production at level four, Handiwork and Gathering at level three, and Transporting at level two. That is a full farm in one Pal.

sections.heading: Elgrove and Vaelet: Grass power
sections.script: Grass Pals do more than farm. Elgrove has a partner skill called Mother Nature's Menace. When you activate it, your attack type changes to Grass and your Attack rises by thirty to fifty percent. That is one of the biggest boosts in this video. At base, Elgrove is a flexible worker, with Planting, Lumbering and Transporting at level three, and Gathering and Mining at level two. Vaelet is the loot Pal. Its skill, Purification of Gaia, makes Ground Pals drop forty to eighty percent more items when you defeat them, and it does not stack. Vaelet is also a monster at base, with Planting, Handiwork, Gathering and Medicine Production at level three, and Transporting and Farming at level two. If you farm drops, Vaelet pays for itself fast.

sections.heading: Felbat and Hoodle: the Dark pair
sections.script: Dark Pals bring tricks. Felbat has a partner skill called Life Steal. While you fight together, both you and Felbat restore five to nine percent of the damage you deal as health. That makes long boss fights much easier. At base Felbat works Medicine Production at level three, so it can brew healing items for you too. Hoodle is cheaper and simpler. Its skill, Void-Dweller, raises the damage you deal to enemies that are not in combat by fifty to one hundred percent, and it does not stack. That makes it a great opener. Sneak up on a target, land a big hit before the fight starts, and then switch to your main team. At base Hoodle works Handiwork and Transporting at level one, which is fine for a starter base.

sections.heading: Galeclaw and Tombat: the explorers
sections.script: If you love exploring, these two are for you. Galeclaw has a partner skill called Galeclaw Glider. While it is in your party, it changes how your equipped glider works. You get high speed gliding, and you can even shoot with your right hand while you glide. At base it works Gathering at level two. Tombat is a scout. Its skill, Ultrasonic Sensor, uses ultrasonic waves to detect nearby dungeons, treasure chests and scrap when you activate it. At base Tombat works Mining at level three, with Gathering and Transporting at level two. Put these two together and you can cover huge areas of the map, find loot quickly, and glide back to your base. Which one would you bring on your next exploration run?

sections.heading: Tarantriss: the web mount
sections.script: Tarantriss deserves its own section. It is a Dark Pal with a partner skill called Tarantriss Web. You can ride it, and while mounted you can double jump. You can also shoot spider web to grapple and move at high speed, which makes it one of the most fun mounts in the game. At base Tarantriss works Handiwork and Gathering at level three, and Medicine Production and Transporting at level two. That is a very useful spread for a Pal that also carries you across the map. If you like fast, vertical movement, this is the mount to try. Compare it with the other mounts in this video. Pyrin is a Fire mount with a Fire attack boost, Azurobe crosses water, and Polapup rules the snow. Tarantriss is the grappling specialist.

sections.heading: How to pick the right partner skill
sections.script: With so many options, how do you choose? Start with your goal. If you want more damage, look at Elgrove for Grass, Pyrin or Azurobe while mounted, and Hoodle for sneak attacks. If you want survival, Felbat and Petallia are your best picks. If you build a big base, Cinnamoth and Petallia boost the work levels of every other Pal there. If you travel a lot, Galeclaw, Tarantriss, Polapup and Tombat make the trip faster and richer. Remember that many of these boosts do not stack, so bringing two Pals with the same effect gives you nothing extra. Mix different skills instead. Also remember that work levels matter more at base than the skill name, so always check what your Pal can actually do before you move it in.

sections.heading: Which one is your favourite
sections.script: That is fourteen Pals with partner skills worth your time. We covered Rooby, Pyrin, Azurobe, Polapup, Foxcicle, Cinnamoth, Petallia, Elgrove, Vaelet, Felbat, Hoodle, Galeclaw, Tombat and Tarantriss, and every skill and work level was checked against two Pal databases in November twenty twenty six. Palworld may change numbers in future updates, so always trust your in game Pal page for the latest values. Which of these Pals do you already use, and which one are you going to catch next? Tell us in the comments below. If this video helped you, please like it and subscribe to HarryBeast Gaming for more Palworld and Aniimo guides every day. Thanks for watching, and see you in the next one.
